title: The Determinant: How Much a Matrix Stretches Space
hook: What does the determinant of a matrix actually measure - not as a formula, but as something you can see?
objectives: See a 2x2 matrix as a transformation of the whole plane.
Interpret the determinant as the factor by which every area scales.
Explain what a zero or negative determinant means geometrically.

sections.title: A matrix moves the plane
sections.goal: Picture a matrix as a transformation.
sections.explanation: Every point moves; grid lines stay straight, parallel and evenly spaced; the basis vectors land on the matrix's columns.
sections.visual_idea: A grid with i-hat and j-hat warps under the matrix, over a faint copy of the original grid.

sections.title: Follow one square
sections.explanation: The unit square becomes a parallelogram of area 3. That factor is the determinant.
sections.visual_idea: A yellow unit square becomes a parallelogram; the area readout changes from 1 to 3.

sections.title: Every area, the same factor
sections.goal: Generalise from the square to any region.
sections.explanation: Any shape can be tiled by small grid squares, and each of those grows by the same factor, so every area scales by the determinant.
sections.visual_idea: A circle, a triangle and a small square all transform, each labelled times 3.

sections.title: Zero and negative
sections.goal: Connect the formula and the special cases.
sections.explanation: det = ad - bc. A zero determinant squashes the plane onto a line; a negative one flips its orientation.
sections.key_formula: \det\begin{bmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{bmatrix} = ad - bc
sections.visual_idea: The formula with numbers; the plane collapsing onto a line; the square flipping over.

takeaway: The determinant is the area scaling factor of a linear transformation, with its sign recording whether the plane was flipped.

quiz.question: A matrix has determinant 5. A region of area 2 is transformed by it. What is the new area?
quiz.why: Every area scales by the determinant: 2 times 5 is 10.

quiz.question: What does a determinant of zero tell you?
choices: The plane is squashed onto a line or a point
quiz.why: Zero area scaling means everything collapses to lower dimension.

quiz.question: What does a negative determinant mean geometrically?
quiz.why: The sign records orientation; the size of the number still measures the stretch.
